demos.title: Two galaxies colliding
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate two galaxies colliding
demos.about: Two disk galaxies, 48 000 GPU-rendered stars: the prograde disk is torn into tidal tails, the retrograde one survives — Toomre & Toomre's classic result.

demos.title: Double slit, one electron at a time
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the double-slit experiment with single electrons, where the interference pattern builds up one electron at a time
demos.about: A 2D Schrödinger wave passes two nanometre slits; single electrons are drawn from the computed flux and the fringes build up dot by dot (KS p = 0.77), then vanish with a which-path detector.

demos.title: Rutherford's gold foil experiment
demos.prompt: /p-simtor recreate Rutherford's gold foil experiment in 3D: alpha particles hitting a gold foil, and show why it proved the atom has a tiny nucleus
demos.about: Alpha tracks computed in a gold nucleus's Coulomb field at true femtometre scale; counts match 1/sin⁴(θ/2) (χ² p = 0.29); switch to Thomson's atom and every track goes straight.

demos.title: Stern–Gerlach in 3D
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate the Stern–Gerlach experiment in 3D, including several magnets in a row, to show that spin is quantised
demos.about: Silver atoms through one to three magnets; exact spin-½ evolution and the Born rule split the beam into two spots, z→x→z splits again, P(+) = cos²(θ/2).

demos.title: Bubble chamber: π → μ → e
demos.prompt: /p-simtor make a 3D bubble chamber: charged particles curling in a magnetic field, with a pion decaying into a muon and then an electron
demos.about: π⁺ → μ⁺ → e⁺ in liquid hydrogen: Lorentz force with Bethe energy loss, PDG lifetimes and V−A decays; bubbles ∝ 1/β², neutrinos invisible.

demos.title: Stirring a Bose–Einstein condensate until a vortex lattice forms
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show a Bose–Einstein condensate being stirred until quantum vortices appear and form a lattice
demos.about: A stirred condensate (2D Gross–Pitaevskii, computed live) can only spin through identical tiny whirlpools, which settle into a triangular grid; stir faster and more appear.

demos.title: Instantons in the 4D lattice vacuum
demos.prompt: /p-simtor visualise the 4D vacuum of a lattice gauge theory: show instantons as you move through Euclidean time, slice by slice
demos.about: Instantons in a 4D SU(2) lattice vacuum: Monte Carlo, then cooling; topological charge density shown slice by slice through Euclidean time (Q = −1.98).

demos.title: Cavendish experiment: weighing the Earth
demos.prompt: /p-simtor recreate the Cavendish experiment in 3D: weighing the Earth with a torsion balance
demos.about: Cavendish's 1798 torsion balance in 3D: four lead balls twist a wire by about a millimetre, and the computed swing gives G and the Earth's mass (5.97×10²⁴ kg).

demos.title: Hydrogen orbitals in 3D
demos.prompt: /p-simtor visualize the 3D probability clouds of hydrogen orbitals
demos.about: All 55 hydrogen orbitals up to n = 5 as exact 3D probability clouds: a glowing |ψ|² volume plus sampled measurements coloured by the sign of ψ.

demos.title: Black-hole binary inspiral in 3D
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show two black holes spiralling together in 3D
demos.about: Two spinning black holes spiral together while their orbit precesses; the computed gravitational wave spreads out as a spiral. The merger itself is marked not computed.

demos.title: Why galaxies need dark matter
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show why galaxies need dark matter, with a 3D galaxy of 100 000 stars
demos.about: 100 000 stars orbit a Milky-Way model in 3D. Switch off the dark-matter halo and the disk swells from 10 to 39 kpc as stars escape.

demos.title: Electron tunnelling through a wall
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show an electron wave packet tunnelling through a barrier in 2D
demos.about: An electron fired at a wall it cannot climb over: its computed wave splits, and 11.98 % gets through (exact: 11.99 %); a slightly thicker wall lets far less through.

demos.title: Black-body radiation
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate black body radiation
demos.about: Planck's law live: the real colour of hot objects, from the cosmic microwave background to a 40 000 K star.

demos.title: Binary black-hole merger
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate two black holes merging
demos.about: Two black holes spiral together and chirp (post-Newtonian inspiral); the merger itself is honestly marked as not computed.

demos.title: Quark confinement
demos.prompt: /p-simtor explain quark confinement with an interactive, scientifically qualified visualization
demos.about: Lattice gauge theory computes the energy between two colour charges: it keeps rising with distance, so they cannot separate.

demos.title: Why a double pendulum is chaotic
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show why a double pendulum is chaotic
demos.about: Two pendulums started 10⁻⁸ rad apart part ways after about 8 s; the Lyapunov exponent is measured live.

demos.title: Three levels warming up
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how the populations of a three-level quantum system change as it heats up
demos.about: Boltzmann populations of three energy levels as the temperature rises, with the heat-capacity peaks they cause.

demos.title: Lennard-Jones fluid (2D)
demos.prompt: /p-simtor create an interactive Lennard-Jones particle simulation
demos.about: Molecular dynamics of a 2D Lennard-Jones fluid: hot gas, condensing clusters and dense liquid.

demos.title: Brownian motion of a pollen grain
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate Brownian motion of a pollen grain in water
demos.about: Pollen grains jiggle in water; their spread grows as 4Dt, Einstein's relation, and Brown's real observation is one click away.

demos.title: Heating a magnet
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how a magnet loses its magnetism when heated
demos.about: A 128×128 Ising magnet heated past its Curie point: ordered domains break up into noise.

demos.title: Radioactive decay chain, atom by atom
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate a radioactive decay chain atom by atom
demos.about: Radon-222 progeny decaying atom by atom, against the smooth Bateman curves.

demos.title: Salt dissolving in still water
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate how salt dissolves in a glass of water
demos.about: Salt on the bottom of a still glass dissolves in hours, but takes weeks to spread through the water by diffusion.

demos.title: SU(2) gauge field on the 3-sphere
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the SU(2) gauge field as points on the 3-sphere in 4D
demos.about: Every SU(2) link and plaquette as a point on the 3-sphere: a gauge transformation scatters the links while every plaquette trace stays fixed.

demos.title: 4D gauge lattice, projected
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show a 4D spacetime lattice of a gauge theory, with links, plaquettes, a Wilson loop and a Polyakov loop, by rotating it in 4D
demos.about: A periodic 4D lattice rotated in 4D and projected to 3D, with a plaquette, a Wilson loop and a Polyakov loop measured on a live Monte Carlo configuration.

demos.title: Asymptotic freedom and the strong force
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show asymptotic freedom and the strong force
demos.about: α_s(Q) from the 4-loop renormalisation group (PDG 2024 input) next to a live SU(2) lattice showing confinement: area law, Creutz ratio 72σ from zero.

demos.title: Yang–Mills mass gap: lattice evidence
demos.prompt: /p-simtor prove the Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
demos.about: Not a proof (it's a Millennium problem): a lattice measurement of the glueball mass gap in 2+1D SU(2), matching Teper (1999) within 0.4σ.

demos.title: The weak interaction: polarised muon decay
demos.prompt: /p-simtor simulate the weak force
demos.about: Polarised muon decay sampled event by event in V−A theory: parity violation ⟨cos θ⟩ = 1/9, Michel spectra, and the lifetime from G_F to 0.66 ppm.

demos.title: Radical-pair compass
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how birds might sense the Earth's magnetic field with the radical-pair mechanism in cryptochrome
demos.about: Exact spin dynamics of a flavin radical pair: the singlet yield depends on the direction of a 50 µT field (29 % compass contrast); a hypothesis with strong behavioural support, shown with its open questions.

demos.title: Energy transfer in the FMO complex
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how energy moves through the photosynthetic FMO complex, and whether quantum coherence helps
demos.about: Lindblad dynamics of the 7-site FMO complex at its crystal positions: noise-assisted transport peaks at 99 % efficiency, where coherence adds almost nothing over classical hopping.

demos.title: Hydrogen tunnelling in an enzyme
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how enzymes use quantum tunnelling to move hydrogen, and why deuterium is so much slower
demos.about: Hydrogen and deuterium race through the same energy wall (computed eigenstates, 1D double well): hydrogen seeps across ~100× faster, matching the size of the measured isotope effect.

demos.title: Proton tunnelling in a G–C base pair
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how protons can tunnel between DNA base pairs and whether that could cause mutations
demos.about: Löwdin's double proton transfer in a G–C pair: exact double-well levels plus a Lindblad environment. Tunnelling raises the tautomer population 3× over classical, but tautomers live ~20 ps — an estimate, not proof, of a tiny role in mutations.

demos.title: How light twists retinal: the first step of vision
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the first step of vision: how light twists retinal in rhodopsin in 200 femtoseconds through a conical intersection
demos.about: A computed quantum wave packet twists retinal's C11=C12 bond and drops through the funnel where two energy states meet; most comes out trans within 200 fs (Hahn & Stock model).

demos.title: Kármán vortex street
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how wind flowing past a cylinder sheds a vortex street, and how the shedding frequency depends on the Reynolds number
demos.about: Live lattice-Boltzmann flow past a cylinder: the vortex street appears above Re ≈ 47 (fit 47.0) and sheds at St = 0.167 at Re 100 (Williamson: 0.164).

demos.title: Dzhanibekov effect: the flipping wing nut
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the Dzhanibekov effect: why a spinning wing nut in space flips over and over
demos.about: A wing nut spun about its middle axis flips over and over; the measured flip interval 1.769842 s matches the exact elliptic-function value 2K(m)/λ to 4×10⁻⁹.

demos.title: The expanding universe
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the universe expanding from the Big Bang to today, with galaxies moving apart and their light stretching, and how we know it is 13.8 billion years old; explain it so someone without a science background understands
demos.about: Space stretches, carrying galaxies apart and stretching their light; running the measured expansion backwards gives the age, 13.79 billion years (Planck: 13.787 ± 0.020).

demos.title: Two solitary waves colliding in a canal
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show two solitary water waves colliding in a shallow canal and passing through each other unchanged
demos.about: Two KdV solitary waves in a canal pass through each other unchanged except for position jumps of +1.238 m and −2.526 m, matching Hirota's exact solution to 10⁻⁶.

demos.title: Laser cavity: mirrors and stability
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how a laser cavity's mirrors shape the light beam and when the cavity becomes unstable
demos.about: Curved mirrors trap light in a beam whose shape they set (computed Gaussian mode and bouncing ray); pull them past the limit and the light walks off.

demos.title: The Chandrasekhar limit
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show why white dwarfs cannot be heavier than about 1.4 solar masses
demos.about: Cold white dwarfs from the exact relativistic electron pressure: mass levels off at 1.456 M☉ (μe = 2) as the radius shrinks; Sirius B's radius reproduced within 0.7σ.

demos.title: Dam break: how fast the flood front moves
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show what happens when a dam breaks and how fast the flood front moves
demos.about: A shallow-water dam break against the exact Ritter/Stoker solutions: the 10 cm flood front runs at 16.81 m/s (exact 16.835), and a rough bed slows it to 5.1 m/s.

demos.title: Spacetime storm: inspiral
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the nonlinear dynamics of curved spacetime from Kip Thorne's colloquium "Geometrodynamics: The Nonlinear Dynamics of Curved Spacetime"
demos.about: Two black holes spiral together; the stretch and squeeze of space around them streams out as spiral gravitational waves. The inspiral is computed; the merger is not.

demos.title: Lagrange points
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show the Lagrange points where the James Webb Space Telescope and the Trojan asteroids stay in step with a planet; explain it so someone without a science background understands
demos.about: Five spots keep pace with a planet: push everything a little and objects at L1/L2 (where Webb works) slide off, while L4/L5 and the Trojan swarm hold.

demos.title: A planet crossing its star
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how astronomers find planets around other stars by watching a star dim when a planet passes in front of it; explain it so someone without a science background understands
demos.about: A planet crossing its star (HD 209458 b, the first found this way) blocks a little light; the computed dip and its length match the measured transit.

demos.title: How Jupiter tore comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 apart
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how Jupiter's gravity tore comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 apart before its pieces crashed into Jupiter in 1994; explain it so someone without a science background understands
demos.about: A 1.5 km rubble comet (500 computed grains) passes 1.33 Jupiter radii from Jupiter in July 1992; the tide beats its own gravity and it breaks into a line of pieces.

demos.title: How spiral arms form
demos.prompt: /p-simtor show how spiral arms form in a galaxy; explain it so someone without a science background understands
demos.about: 30 000 stars pulling on each other (particle-mesh N-body) turn small clumps into spiral arms, traffic jams that stars drift through; switch off their pull and the disk stays smooth.
